newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, swaps ease.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, swaps ease.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in slow late trading on Tuesday.
Dealers said operators calmed down as overnight money fell to 9.5/10.0 percent as expected in the afternoon from an early high of 13.0 percent on a relatively tight market.
One U.S. bank dealer said there was not much going on, with operators keeping sentiment firm on the rupiah.
Spot rupiah was at 2,371.75/72.25 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,372.0/72.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,371.00/71.75 and 2,371.40/71.70, respectively.
The U.S. bank dealer said swap rates were easing slightly on speculation that liquidity would not be tight on Friday because of large amount of maturing central bank papers (SBIs).
Dealers said operators seemed to have factored in liquidity would be tight in the short-term and would turn ample after the Lunar New Year and Eid al-Fitr celebration early next month.
One European bank dealer said some operators seemed to have gone short in longer-term swaps based on that assumption.
"They are covering with short-term swaps, keeping those rates relatively high despite an easing in the money market."
The dealer said swap rates were inching up from Monday but the rates were slightly lower from the morning levels.
Overnight swap was at 0.50/0.55 and tom/next at 0.60/0.65.
One-month swaps were at 13.20/13.50, two at 23.50/24.50, three at 37.00/37.50 and six at 74.00/74.75 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,370/2.562 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,370/2,418 on Tuesday.
The central bank depreciated the rupiah by only two points last week after lowering it by four points the previous week.
